title: Relative pseudo-coherence checked in a flat ambient scheme
statement: Let $X\xrightarrow{i}P\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with $i$ a closed immersion and $P\to S$ flat and locally of finite presentation [def-pc-morphism-conventions, def-weil-flat-morphism]. For every $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], $E$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $S$ [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex] if and only if $Ri_*E$ is pseudo-coherent on $P$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image, def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex]. There is no quasi-compactness, properness or Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 09UU, lemma-check-relative-pseudo-coherence-on-charts, equivalence (1) and (3) for every integer m

proof.text: First $X$ and $P$ are locally of finite type over $S$ in [def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Indeed, on affine neighbourhoods for $P\to S$, a finitely presented algebra $B$ is generated by finitely many elements over the base ring $R$. The inverse image under $i$ is affine with ring $B/I$, by the affine characterization of a closed immersion. The same generators generate $B/I$ over $R$. These neighbourhoods cover $X$. Also $i$ induces a homeomorphism onto a closed subset, by definition.

source.place: 09UU hypotheses; definitions of local finite presentation and closed immersion

proof.text: Put $F=Ri_*E\in D(\mathcal O_P)$ and fix $m\in\mathbf Z$. Apply the closed-immersion statement [lem-sfb-closed-support-relative-pseudocoherence] to $i$ to obtain $E$ relatively $m$-pseudo-coherent over $S$ if and only if $F$ is. By [lem-sfb-flat-lfp-structure-relative-pseudocoherence], $\mathcal O_P[0]$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $S$. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-pseudocoherence-composition] to $\mathrm{id}_P:P\to P$ and $F$: relative $m$-pseudo-coherence of $F$ over $S$ is equivalent to relative $m$-pseudo-coherence over $P$. All local finite type hypotheses hold by step 1 and the identity map.

source.place: Tag 09UU, proof: (1) iff (2) using 09VG in place of 09UK; (2) iff (3) using 09UT and 0695

proof.text: For the identity of $P$, [lem-sfb-relative-pseudocoherence-all-affine-charts] shows that relative $m$-pseudo-coherence of $F$ implies absolute $m$-pseudo-coherence in [def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex]: on every affine open $V\subset P$ take $U=V$, $n=0$ and $j=\mathrm{id}_V:V\to\mathbf A^0_V=V$. Here [def-nagata-relative-affine-space] gives $\mathbf A^0_V=V$ since the polynomial ring in zero variables is the base ring. The derived direct image of the identity is the identity. Conversely, take the local maps $\alpha_c:P_c^\bullet\to F|_{W_c}$ of that absolute definition, with cohomology isomorphisms above $m$ and a surjection at $m$. Refine the opens $W_c$ by affine opens $V$. For an open inclusion $k$, $\mathcal O_V=k^{-1}\mathcal O_{W_c}$, so the formula for $Lk^*$ in [def-pc-derived-pullback] reduces to termwise restriction: tensoring over the same ring sheaf is the identity. Restriction is exact on stalks and preserves finite free modules and their direct summands. Thus it preserves the strictly perfect complexes of [def-pc-perfect-complex] and the stated cohomology conditions. For the relative definition use this affine cover on both source and base, with $n=0$ and identity embeddings. These give its required witnesses. Hence relative and absolute $m$-pseudo-coherence agree for the identity of $P$.

source.place: Tags 09UJ and 09VC for the forward implication; Tag 09UI for the reverse; cohomology.tex Tags 08CB and 08CC for local derived strictly perfect approximations and their open restrictions

proof.text: Combining steps 2 and 3 gives the desired equivalence for each integer $m$. Quantify over all $m$: relative pseudo-coherence is defined by these conditions for every $m$, and absolute pseudo-coherence is likewise equivalent to absolute $m$-pseudo-coherence of [def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex] for every $m$. This proves both directions for the original arbitrary $E$. The affine covers may vary with $m$; no uniform bound or finite cover is used.
